# `property-became-write-only`

Property became writeOnly

| | |
|---|---|
| **Kind** | `wire` |
| **Default severity** | `info` in requests, `error` in responses |
| **Rule IDs** | `property-became-write-only` (both directions), `property-became-write-only-in-request`, `property-became-write-only-in-response` |
| **Status** | Implemented (M5) |
| **Group** | Schemas ([RULES.md section 7](../../RULES.md)) |

## What it detects

`writeOnly: true` was added to a property, so it is no longer returned in responses.

## Why this default

In requests: nothing changes. In responses: clients that read it get nothing.

## Example

From test case [`property-became-write-only`](../../test/cases/property-became-write-only/): A response property became writeOnly: it is no longer returned.

`openapi.yaml`, base → revision:

```diff
  …
          secret:
            type: string
+           writeOnly: true
```

Findings:

- `property-became-write-only-in-response` · error · #/components/schemas/Pet

## Test cases

The example above is the only test case for this rule.


## Policy options

Every rule takes `severity` (`error`, `warn`, `info` or `off`), `fix` and `explanation` in the policy file, for the generic ID or any variant ID above (the more specific ID wins). The policy file arrives in M6; see [POLICY.md](../../POLICY.md).

```yaml
rules:
  property-became-write-only: error
```

## How to fix

Keep returning the property until clients stop reading it.
